Fit on historical features and forecast future features

Source: R/feature-pipeline.R
feature_forecast.Rd

feature_forecast() runs a feature_pipeline() separately on the historical data and on the future data, then hands the two feature tables to a pair of modelling functions:

  • fit(history_features, y, ...) receives the historical features and the response aligned with them,

  • predict(model, future_features, ...) receives only the future features.

The tables handed to the model are the very tables returned in history, future and forecast, so what the model sees is what is delivered. The historical table is aligned on its own key and index, and the future table on its own; features are never borrowed across series or across time points.

Usage

feature_forecast(
  .data,
  pipeline,
  new_data,
  fit,
  predict,
  y,
  fit_args = list(),
  predict_args = list(),
  pred_name = ".pred"
)

Arguments

.data

A tsibble holding the response and the raw inputs.

pipeline

A feature_pipeline().

new_data

The future table: a data frame holding the key, the index and any known future inputs, or a number of future observations to generate with new_data(). It must not contain the response.

fit

A function of the historical features and the response, as in fit(history_features, y, ...).

predict

A function of the fitted model and the future features, as in predict(model, future_features, ...).

y

The response column in .data.

fit_args, predict_args

Lists of additional arguments passed on to fit and predict.

pred_name

The column name used for the predictions when predict() returns a vector.

Value

A list of class tsbl_feature_forecast with elements

  • history: the historical feature tsibble,

  • future: the future feature tsibble,

  • forecast: a tsibble covering every future key/index pair with the predictions,

  • model: the object returned by fit,

  • features: a list of the history and future feature tables,

  • pipeline: the pipeline that was run.

See also

compute_features()

Examples

library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
tsbl <- tsibble(
  id = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 6), t = rep(1:6, 2),
  y = c(1:6, 3:8), x = c(2:7, 4:9), key = id, index = t
)
trend <- feature_node(
  "trend", function(x) mutate(x, trend = as.numeric(t)),
  outputs = "trend", inputs = "t"
)
future <- new_data(tsbl, n = 2)
future <- as_tsibble(future, key = id, index = t)
future
#> # A tsibble: 4 x 2 [1]
#> # Key:       id [2]
#>   id        t
#>   <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 a         7
#> 2 a         8
#> 3 b         7
#> 4 b         8
res <- feature_forecast(
  tsbl, feature_pipeline(trend), future,
  fit = function(h, y) lm(y ~ trend, data = mutate(as_tibble(h), y = y)),
  predict = function(m, f) predict(m, newdata = as_tibble(f)),
  y = y
)
res$forecast
#> # A tsibble: 4 x 3 [1]
#> # Key:       id [2]
#>   id        t .pred
#>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 a         7     8
#> 2 a         8     9
#> 3 b         7     8
#> 4 b         8     9
